title: She grew up in India, studied at Osmania University - and just won Harvard's highest honor for alumni. November 16, 2026.
excerpt: From a 19-year-old revolutionary whose example outlived him by three decades, to an immunologist whose Hyderabad education carried her to Harvard's top honor, November 16's two stories are about foundations that keep paying forward.
bodyHtml:
Today's two stories span over a century, but share a thread: a foundation built early that kept carrying weight long after.

He was executed at 19 for plotting an armed uprising against British rule. Bhagat Singh later carried his photo

Kartar Singh Sarabha, a Ghadar Party revolutionary, was hanged at Lahore Central Jail on November 16, 1915, at age 19, convicted in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. Bhagat Singh is said to have carried his photograph and considered him a personal hero - carrying his example into the next generation of India's independence movement.

She grew up in India, studied at Osmania University - and just won Harvard's highest honor for alumni

Dr. Anjana Rao, born in Washington, DC but raised in India, earned her bachelor's and master's degrees at Osmania University in Hyderabad before going to Harvard for her PhD in biophysics. Now a professor at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology and UC San Diego, she was named a 2026 Harvard Centennial Medalist for her work co-discovering how genes switch on inside immune cells.

Two stories, one pattern: an example that outlived the person who set it, and an education that kept paying forward decades later.
